---
title: "Exclusion rules"
execute:
  cache: false
---

The [ManyBabies 1 release](units-of-assignment.qmd) is the output of a sequential exclusion pipeline. The paper describes participant rules, session-level errors, trial-level errors, a minimum included looking time, and a laboratory inclusion rule. The official script then completes every retained infant to sixteen possible test-trial rows. Consequently, a row without an included looking time need not represent one single event.

```{r}
manybabies <- readRDS("data/manybabies/manybabies1-trials.rds")

stopifnot(
  nrow(manybabies) == 37264L,
  length(unique(manybabies$infant_id)) == 2329L,
  sum(manybabies$trial_missing) == 10369L,
  sum(!manybabies$trial_metadata_observed) == 4383L,
  all(is.na(manybabies$looking_time_seconds) == manybabies$trial_missing)
)
```

## Retention enters the estimand

Let $R_r=1$ when possible trial row $r$ contains a looking time retained by the released pipeline and let $R_r=0$ otherwise. A row-weighted register contrast among retained outcomes is

$$
\Delta_{R=1}
=\mathbb{E}[Y_r\mid Z_r=\mathrm{IDS},R_r=1]
-\mathbb{E}[Y_r\mid Z_r=\mathrm{ADS},R_r=1].
$$

This quantity conditions on retention. It differs from an equally weighted [within-infant contrast](within-participant-designs.qmd), a contrast over all planned trials, and a contrast over outcomes made missing by later events.

Exclusion is thus not merely table cleaning. It helps define the population of responses represented by an analysis.

## Three row states in the teaching table

The two released indicators separate rows with included looking time, rows with trial metadata but no included looking time, and completed rows without trial metadata.

```{r}
row_state <- ifelse(
  !manybabies$trial_missing,
  "included looking time",
  ifelse(
    manybabies$trial_metadata_observed,
    "trial metadata but no included looking time",
    "completed row without trial metadata"
  )
)

row_state_counts <- as.data.frame(
  table(state = row_state),
  responseName = "rows"
)
row_state_counts$proportion <- row_state_counts$rows / nrow(manybabies)

knitr::kable(
  row_state_counts,
  digits = 4,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Across all `r format(nrow(manybabies), big.mark = ",")` possible rows, `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(!manybabies$trial_missing))` retain an included looking time. Restricting the denominator to the `r format(sum(manybabies$trial_metadata_observed), big.mark = ",")` rows with recorded trial metadata raises the retained share to `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(!manybabies$trial_missing[manybabies$trial_metadata_observed]))`.

These states should not be collapsed into a causal explanation. A missing included outcome may follow an error-marked trial, the minimum-looking-time rule, or termination before a later trial. A completed row without metadata records a possible opportunity added by the official completion step. The final RDS does not retain a unique original reason for every missing row.

## Register and analysis-set margins

For rows whose trial metadata were recorded, the missing proportion can be computed by register.

```{r}
missing_by_register <- aggregate(
  trial_missing ~ register,
  data = manybabies[manybabies$trial_metadata_observed, ],
  FUN = mean
)
names(missing_by_register)[2L] <- "missing_proportion"

knitr::kable(missing_by_register, digits = 4)
```

The observed-metadata missing proportions are `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * missing_by_register$missing_proportion[missing_by_register$register == "ADS"])` for ADS and `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * missing_by_register$missing_proportion[missing_by_register$register == "IDS"])` for IDS. This difference is descriptive. It does not identify why an outcome is missing.

An exclusion rule can also operate at the infant level by requiring a minimum number of included trials. We can examine the thresholds considered in the paper's sensitivity analysis without reversing the official pipeline.

```{r}
usable_by_infant <- aggregate(
  as.integer(!trial_missing) ~ infant_id,
  data = manybabies,
  FUN = sum
)
names(usable_by_infant)[2L] <- "usable_trials"

usable_thresholds <- 2^(1:3)
threshold_retention <- data.frame(
  minimum_usable_trials = usable_thresholds,
  retained_infants = vapply(
    usable_thresholds,
    function(threshold) sum(usable_by_infant$usable_trials >= threshold),
    integer(1)
  ),
  total_infant_identifiers = nrow(usable_by_infant)
)
threshold_retention$retained_proportion <- with(
  threshold_retention,
  retained_infants / total_infant_identifiers
)

knitr::kable(
  threshold_retention,
  digits = 4,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Requiring at least `r paste(usable_thresholds, collapse = ", ")` included trials retains `r paste(format(threshold_retention$retained_infants, big.mark = ","), collapse = ", ")` infant identifiers, respectively. Changing the threshold changes the analysis set and may change the population of infants represented by the estimate.

## Missing outcomes over the session

The released missing indicator can be summarized over trial position and observed testing method. The three lines are descriptive because method is tied to laboratory practices, populations, age coverage, and implementation.

```{r}
missing_by_method_trial <- aggregate(
  trial_missing ~ method + trial_number,
  data = manybabies,
  FUN = mean
)
names(missing_by_method_trial)[3L] <- "missing_proportion"

stopifnot(
  all(missing_by_method_trial$missing_proportion >= 0),
  all(missing_by_method_trial$missing_proportion <= 1)
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "Proportion of rows without included looking time over trial number, separately for each observed testing method."

ggplot2::ggplot(
  missing_by_method_trial,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = trial_number,
    y = missing_proportion,
    linetype = method
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(color = "grey25", linewidth = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "grey25", size = 1.2) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%"),
    limits = c(0, 0.72)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(
      min(missing_by_method_trial$trial_number),
      4L * seq_len(max(missing_by_method_trial$trial_number) / 4L)
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Trial number",
    y = "Rows without included looking time",
    linetype = "Method"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The rise over position may reflect termination, attention, procedure, or their combination. The plot alone cannot separate these mechanisms. It also cannot estimate an effect of assigning a testing method because method was not assigned.

## Reporting the flow without overreconstruction

A reconstructible design report should distinguish (i) original participant exclusions, (ii) session- or trial-level error decisions, (iii) the minimum-looking-time rule, and (iv) rows created to represent later possible trials. The primary paper and official scripts document the first three stages. The teaching RDS records their final consequences through `trial_missing` and preserves the completion distinction through `trial_metadata_observed`.

The release cannot be run backward to recover the original cause of every absent outcome. Sensitivity analyses may vary a defensible minimum-trial rule, but they should not relabel the resulting selection as if it were the original recruitment flow.

::: {.callout-note title="Audit the released analysis set"}
1. What population of rows is described by $\Delta_{R=1}$?
2. Why are a recorded trial without an included outcome and a completed row without metadata distinct?
3. What changes when the minimum usable-trial threshold increases?
4. Why can the method-specific curves not be interpreted causally?
:::

The inclusion and exclusion pipeline defines which infant-trial outcomes enter the comparison. The final page carries this design forward by fitting an empirical model and using its effect and variance estimates to calibrate [power by simulation](power-by-simulation.qmd).
